title: C# Multiple Choice Questions - Delegates
description: This section of our 1000+ C# MCQs focuses in detail on delegates in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: The 'ref' parameter modifier can be used with which of the following in C#?
questions.explanation: The 'ref' keyword is a parameter modifier. It can be used in the signature of any method, whether it is declared as static or instance.

questions.question: Which of the following is a necessary condition to use a delegate in C#?
questions.explanation: To implement a delegate, you must first define the delegate type, which specifies the signature of the methods it can encapsulate.

questions.question: Suppose a Generic class 'SortObjects' needs to sort objects of any type. Which programming construct is best suited to implement a custom comparison function passed to it?
questions.explanation: Delegates are ideal for passing methods as arguments. A comparison delegate (like Comparison<T>) allows a sorting algorithm to be decoupled from the logic of how objects are compared.

questions.question: Which programming construct should be used to implement a notification mechanism for an object at runtime in C#?
questions.explanation: Delegates (and Events, which are built on delegates) provide a way for an object to notify other objects when something happens, acting as a callback mechanism.

questions.question: Which of the following is an INCORRECT statement about delegates in C#?
questions.explanation: In C#, delegates are reference types (derived from System.Delegate), they are object-oriented (storing both the method and the object target), and they are type-safe (signature must match).

questions.question: What happens internally when you declare a delegate like 'delegate void Del(int i);'?

options.text: The compiler creates a class named 'Del'
The 'Del' class is implicitly derived from MulticastDelegate
The generated class contains an Invoke() method and a constructor

questions.explanation: The 'delegate' keyword is shorthand for defining a class that inherits from System.MulticastDelegate. The compiler generates the necessary members, including the Invoke method.

questions.question: Which of the following is an incorrect statement about delegates?

options.text: A single delegate can invoke more than one method (multicast)
Delegates can be shared between objects
Delegates are type-safe wrappers for function pointers
A delegate is a value type

questions.explanation: Delegates are reference types in C#. They store a reference to a method and, optionally, a reference to a class instance.

questions.question: How does a delegate in C# differ from a conventional function pointer in C++?

options.text: C# delegates are true objects in the Common Type System
Delegates can encapsulate both static and instance methods

questions.explanation: Unlike C++ function pointers, C# delegates are type-safe, object-oriented, and can seamlessly handle instance methods by storing the 'this' reference.

questions.question: Choose the INCORRECT statement about delegates:

options.text: Delegates can be used for callback notifications

questions.explanation: One of the key features of C# delegates is their type safety; the compiler ensures that the method assigned to a delegate exactly matches the delegate's signature.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about a delegate?

options.text: Inheritance is a prerequisite for using delegates
Delegates provide object-oriented wrappers for function pointers

questions.explanation: A delegate is an object-oriented, type-safe, and secure wrapper for a method pointer.
